title: History's Plot Twists
blurb: Presidents, explorers and inventors did weirder stuff than any movie. One per card is cap.

cards.say: Thomas Jefferson [trained a pet mockingbird to take food from between his lips], [served as the first vice president, under George Washington], [sold about 6,500 of his own books to Congress after the British burned its library], and [was the first president sworn in at Washington, D.C.].
cards.real: John Adams was Washington's vice president. Jefferson was his secretary of state, and later the second vice president, under Adams.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_the_Mockingbird (trained Dick to take food from between his lips)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Jefferson (first secretary of state, 1790 to 1793; vice president 1797 to 1801, under John Adams)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Jefferson (sold his library, nearly 6,500 volumes, after the British burned the Library of Congress)

cards.say: John Quincy Adams [kept a diary for almost 70 years of his life], [worked for an American diplomat in Russia when he was 14], [served 17 years in the House of Representatives after being president], and [won more electoral votes than anyone else in the 1824 election].
cards.real: Andrew Jackson won the most electoral votes in 1824, 99 to 84, but not a majority, so the House of Representatives chose Adams.

cards.say: William Howard Taft [had the West Wing rebuilt after a fire on Christmas Eve], [became chief justice of the Supreme Court after being president], [began the tradition of presidents throwing out baseball's first pitch, in 1910], and [kept a cow named Pauline on the White House lawn].
cards.real: The West Wing burned on Christmas Eve 1929, under Herbert Hoover. Taft's West Wing work came in 1909, when he enlarged it and added the first Oval Office.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House (fire on Christmas Eve 1929, under Hoover; Taft expanded the West Wing and created the first Oval Office in 1909)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceremonial_first_pitch (the tradition of presidential first pitches began with Taft in 1910)
https://www.livescience.com/24563-first-paws-history-of-presidential-pets.html (Pauline Wayne, a Holstein that grazed the White House lawn)

cards.say: Herbert Hoover [spoke Chinese with his wife in the White House to keep their talks private], [was a student in Stanford University's very first class], [was the first president born in California], and [was the first president with a telephone on his desk].
cards.real: Hoover was born in West Branch, Iowa, in 1874, which made him the first president born west of the Mississippi River.
src: https://www.meridian.org/pathtoharmony/gallery/17/ (the Hoovers spoke Chinese for private talks in the White House); https://www.hooverminthorn.org/?p=1207 (the same)
https://www.history.com/articles/10-things-you-may-not-know-about-herbert-hoover (a member of Stanford's inaugural class, 1891); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbert_Hoover (Pioneer Class)
https://www.history.com/articles/10-things-you-may-not-know-about-herbert-hoover (born in West Branch, Iowa; the first president born west of the Mississippi)
https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/1929-nobody-thought-president-needed-telephone-his-office-180962646/ (Hoover had the first phone put on the president's desk in 1929)

cards.say: Christopher Columbus [was sent back to Spain in chains in 1500], [used a predicted eclipse of the Moon to get food in Jamaica], [insisted for the rest of his life that he had reached Asia], and [sailed home from his first voyage aboard the Santa Maria].
cards.real: The Santa Maria ran aground off Hispaniola on Christmas Day 1492, so Columbus sailed home on the smaller Niña instead.
src: https://www.britannica.com/biography/Christopher-Columbus/The-first-voyage (Santa María ran aground December 25, 1492); https://www.history.com/articles/christopher-columbus-ships (Columbus sailed back to Spain on the Niña)

cards.say: Marco Polo [came home to Venice after 24 years away], [brought pasta back to Italy for the first time], [told the story of his travels to a cellmate in prison], and [had a travel book that later inspired Christopher Columbus].
cards.real: Italy had pasta before Marco Polo got home in 1295: a soldier in Genoa left a basket of macaroni in his belongings back in 1279.

cards.say: Lewis and Clark [were the first explorers to cross North America to the Pacific], [brought along a big Newfoundland dog named Seaman], [packed 193 pounds of dried portable soup for the trip], and [let Sacagawea and an enslaved man named York vote on where to move their camp].
cards.real: Alexander Mackenzie's party crossed Canada to the Pacific in 1793, twelve years before Lewis and Clark got there.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewis_and_Clark_Expedition (Mackenzie crossed from Quebec to the Pacific 1792 to 1793; the expedition reached the Pacific in November 1805)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewis_and_Clark_Expedition (Seaman, the only animal to finish the trip)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewis_and_Clark_Expedition (Sacagawea and York both took part in the November 1805 vote on moving the camp)

cards.say: Julius Caesar [was once kidnapped by pirates and held for ransom], [made the year 46 BC last 445 days], [was the first emperor of ancient Rome], and [had the month of July named after him].
cards.real: Caesar ruled Rome as dictator but was never emperor. His adopted heir, Augustus, became the first Roman emperor after Caesar died.

cards.say: Alexander the Great [was born in the Greek city of Athens], [was taught by the philosopher Aristotle until he was 16], [named a city after his horse, Bucephalas], and [never lost a single battle he fought].
cards.real: Alexander was born in 356 BC in Pella, the capital of the kingdom of Macedon. Athens was a separate city-state far to the south.

cards.say: Thomas Edison [got his very first patent for an electric vote counter], [started losing his hearing when he was about 12], [earned more than 1,000 patents in the United States], and [invented the very first electric light bulb].
cards.real: Inventors like Joseph Swan made electric bulbs before Edison. His big step was a long-lasting, practical bulb that could be sold.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Edison (developed hearing problems at the age of 12)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Edison (many incandescent lamps were devised before Edison; Joseph Swan's similar lamp)

cards.say: Alexander Graham Bell [wanted people to answer the phone by saying ahoy], [built a boat that set a world speed record of over 70 miles per hour], [made his first telephone call to his mother], and [sent a voice message on a beam of light in 1880].
cards.real: Bell's first call, on March 10, 1876, was to his assistant Thomas Watson in another room, asking him to come over.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahoy (Bell first suggested ahoy as the telephone greeting)
https://www.britannica.com/list/6-fast-facts-about-alexander-graham-bell (HD-4 hit 70.8 mph in 1919, a speed record)

https://webarchive.library.unt.edu/eot2008/20090812232405/http://memory.loc.gov/ammem/bellhtml/bell1.html (Library of Congress page, archived: Bell's March 10, 1876 notebook, Watson in another room); https://www.mentalfloss.com/article/81620/10-amazing-facts-about-alexander-graham-bell (the same)

cards.say: The ancient Olympic Games [were held every four years for more than 1,000 years], [ended with a long marathon race of about 26 miles], [crowned a cook as their first champion on record], and [listed a woman from Sparta as a winner of the chariot race].
cards.real: The marathon was invented for the first modern Olympics in 1896, by a French scholar named Michel Bréal. The ancient Games never had one.
